newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-LAZIO ALL BUT GIVE UP CHASE FOR RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAZIO ALL BUT GIVE UP CHASE FOR RONALDO.

text.p: Lazio owner Sergio Cragnotti made clear on Sunday he had abandoned almost all hope of signing Brazil's Ronaldo after talks with the player's agents that signalled he was set to stay at Barcelona.
"I don't know the details but the agents informed me that the negotiations with Barcelona are heading towards a conclusion," Cragnotti said at Rome airport on his return from Brazil.
"I said we are still available and that I'm here if anything comes up."
Cragnotti said agents Reinaldo Pitta and Alexandre Martins, whom he met in Sao Paolo, had acknowledged the seriousness of Lazio's offer.
Although he said he still retained "some hope" of signing the player, he added: "Ronaldo wants Barcelona. The club has given him a lot and it's the first side on his mind."

Rome club Lazio, fifth in Italy's serie A, emerged as frontrunners last month in the chase to sign Ronaldo, the world player of the year, following newspaper reports that Barcelona were ready to let him leave for $32 million.
Cragnotti meanwhile said he had reached a agreement to bring Argentine midfielder Matias Almeyda to Lazio in a transfer worth $7.7 million.
Almeyda will move from financially-stretched Spanish club Sevilla who paid Argentina's River Plate a club record $10 million for the player earlier in the season and still owe part of the fee.
"We have a deal for Almeyda and there aren't going to be any problems," Cragnotti said.
